wiki_text: Kuwait Integrated Petroleum Industries Company (KIPIC), the Kuwait Petroleum Corporation (KPC) subsidiary that developed and had operated the Al-Zour LNG import terminal since it entered service in 2022, was formally dissolved and merged into Kuwait National Petroleum Company (KNPC) following a Supreme Petroleum Council decision reported by regional press in mid-2026 (Kuwait Times, AGBI, Zawya, Times Kuwait, all April-July 2026). As a result, KNPC is now the correct current owner/parent entity for the Al-Zour LNG complex including the import terminal, consistent with GEM's existing Owner value 'Kuwait National Petroleum Co [100%]'. Day-to-day operation and maintenance of the LNG import terminal itself has been contracted since Dec 2020 to DESFA (Greece's gas transmission system operator), part of a Snam/Enagas-led O&M consortium; DESFA's first O&M year began 1 May 2022 and DESFA was still confirmed active as the terminal's O&M contractor as of a Feb 2025 Times Kuwait report.

topic: Explorer FSRU — vessel identity and current deployment
wiki_text: The 'Explorer' FSRU that formerly served Mina Al-Ahmadi (2009-2013/2014) is identifiable via maritime tracking registries as IMO 9361079, built 2008, commercially managed by Excelerate Energy LP. GEM's schema has no FloatingVesselIMO column, so this identifier cannot be staged as a structured field. As of early 2026, per Excelerate Energy's own project listings and fleet tracking, this vessel is deployed elsewhere (UAE) and not associated with any active or planned Kuwait project. No evidence found of any Explorer/Excelerate return to Mina Al-Ahmadi.

topic: Golar Igloo FSRU — vessel identity and current deployment (post-Kuwait)
wiki_text: The 'Golar Igloo' FSRU that served Mina Al-Ahmadi from delivery (Feb 2014) until departure in 2022 is identifiable as IMO 9633991. GEM's schema has no FloatingVesselIMO column, so this cannot be staged as a structured field. After leaving Kuwait, the vessel transited via Rotterdam (arrived 28 Aug 2022) en route to the Netherlands, and has since been renamed 'Energos Igloo' (following New Fortress Energy's acquisition of the Golar Igloo and sister vessels), deployed at the EemsEnergy Terminal (Eemshaven), Netherlands, where it resumed regasification activity per a Jan 2023 LinkedIn post from an LNG industry analyst (Alex Froley) referencing EemsEnergyTerminal's own announcement. This vessel is confirmed NOT associated with any current or planned Kuwait project.
